messages.content: What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
The acceleration of the ball is determined by gravity, not by its initial speed.  
When you throw it straight upward, the only force acting on it (ignoring air resistance) is gravity pulling it downward. That gives a constant acceleration of  

**\(a = -9.8 \text{ m/s}^2\)**  

(The negative sign indicates the direction is downward.)  

So regardless of whether you start at 5 m/s or any other speed, the acceleration remains –9.8 m/s².
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?" They want the acceleration. But acceleration is constant due to gravity: -9.8 m/s^2 downward. The question might be misphrased: maybe they want the maximum height? But they specifically ask acceleration. So answer: acceleration due to gravity is -9.8 m/s^2 (downward). Provide explanation. No function call needed.
